logic_contains: name: build-code-review
Use when defining review rules for a repo
Not for automated security scanning (use secure-supply-chain)
# Code Review Policy
approve once the change improves overall code health and has no unresolved blocking correctness or security issue, even if it is not perfect
There is no perfect code, only better code
About 100 lines changed is a healthy norm, and around 1000 is usually too large
Separate refactors from behavior changes
Stack PRs for big features
approve a change too large to review well
first response within **one business day at most**
Review speed is a team throughput lever
at least 1 owner (from CODEOWNERS) per touched area
second approver for security-sensitive paths, schema migrations, and infra
what changed, why, how it was tested, and the risk and rollback
self-review before requesting review and keep CI green
leave style nits to formatters and linters
Humans review design
check in priority order: design, functionality, complexity, tests, security and privacy, naming and comments and docs, operability
does it fit the architecture and the ADRs
concurrency, user impact
over-engineered for needs that do not exist yet
correct, meaningful, and able to fail
authz, secrets, PII, injection
logging, metrics, failure modes, flags
comment on the code, not the person, and explain why
`blocking:`, `nit:`, `optional:`, `question:`, `fyi:`
Escalate to the lead (team-lead) after one round
set-review-policy:
apply policy baseline with current as policy
branch protection, and PR template
if reviewed is too large to review well:
asking the author to split the oversized change
generate findings in checklist priority order
verify every comment carries a severity label
approve, approve with nits, or request changes, with reasons
approve a change too large to review well
block a change on personal preference that no style guide supports
Make PR age a visible metric
